text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect; MRI_Spine: Information not provided.

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Patient
text: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That explanation doesn't fit your current neurological symptoms; given your confusion and the abnormal lymph nodes, we need to look for infectious or inflammatory causes affecting the nervous system. Have you recently had a fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss?

speaker: Patient

Are you able to recall recent travel, contact with sick individuals, or any new medications?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 9.2 g/dL; Leukocyte_Count: 3600/mm3; Platelet_Count: 140,000/mm3; CD4+_Count: 56/μL; HIV_Viral_Load: > 100,000 copies/mL; ESR: Information not provided; CRP: Information not provided; CT_Abdomen_Pelvis: Information not provided. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) with Neurological Complications (likely CMV encephalitis or HIV-associated dementia given the CD4 count of 56/μL, severe leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and history of white matter lesions).
